documents.title: Learn About Generative AI: Vassar AI Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The guide says "Vassar College does not have an official policy on generative AI but rather empowers Vassar faculty members and departments to make tailored policies". It sets no rule of its own and hands the decision to instructors, so delegates; the student advice (check syllabus, disclose, verify) is guidance, not a stance.
documents.summary: A library research guide stating Vassar has no official AI policy and leaves rules to faculty and departments. It gives students short advice: check the syllabus, ask the professor, disclose and verify AI use, mind privacy, and evaluate tools.

units.why: States as fact that the college has no official AI policy: "does not have an official policy on generative AI". That is the P108 statement that no AI-specific policy exists, a fact, so modality informs.
units.anchor: Vassar College does not have an official policy on generative AI

units.why: Says the college "empowers Vassar faculty members and departments to make tailored policies about AI for their courses". The decision is handed to instructors and departments, so P04; P85 (units set own rules) fits less since the focus is course policy.
units.anchor: empowers Vassar faculty members and departments to make tailored policies about AI
units.fit_note: Also names departments, not only individual instructors.

units.why: Warns that "what's permissible in one class might constitute a violation of the Academic Integrity policy in another class". This is the rule that one course's permissions do not carry over, P11, addressed to students.
units.anchor: what's permissible in one class might constitute a violation of the Academic Integrity policy

units.why: Tells students to "Check the syllabus and course page on Moodle to familiarize yourself with the course AI policy". Students must find and follow each course's rules, which is P78 (not P10, since no doubt is involved yet).
units.anchor: Check the syllabus and course page on Moodle

units.why: "If you have questions about it, or there isn't a policy, talk to your professor." Students unsure or facing silence should ask the instructor, matching P10.
units.anchor: If you have questions about it, or there isn't a policy,

units.why: "If you use generative AI, make sure to disclose your use of AI." A general duty to acknowledge AI use in academic work, P24; "make sure to" is directive but soft, so should.
units.anchor: If you use generative AI, make sure to

units.why: Gives forms disclosure may take: "citing it as a source, describing how you used it in the Methods section of your paper, or something else". It lists acceptable ways of disclosing; P24 fits though it is about format, so a fit note.
units.anchor: citing it as a source, describing how you used it in the Methods section
units.fit_note: Gives example formats only; no required form or tool/prompt details (not P25).

units.why: "It's crucial that you are transparent about how you're using AI" stresses the disclosure duty and asks for how-use detail, not only that AI was used. Same type P24 as the previous unit; this adds the emphasis and the "how" scope.
units.anchor: It's crucial that you are transparent about how you're using AI

units.why: "Critically evaluate the outputs of AI tools" tells students to judge AI output rather than accept it, P31 (AI output can be wrong).
units.anchor: Critically

units.why: "Verify claims; whenever possible, go to the source!" is a verification duty on AI-supplied claims, P31.
units.anchor: Verify claims; whenever possible,

units.why: "Stay informed about the ethical concerns surrounding generative AI so that you can make an informed decision about whether to use it." The aim is weighing ethics before deciding to use AI, so P118 rather than P102 (keeping up with developments).
units.anchor: about the ethical concerns
units.fit_note: Also a duty to stay informed (P102).

units.why: The guide opens by saying it is "designed to support Vassar community members as they navigate decisions about their use of generative AI" and that the topic is "rapidly evolving". A purpose preamble (P56); the note on change is secondary to P54.
units.anchor: designed to support Vassar community members as they navigate decisions about their use
units.frag_start: This guide is designed to support
units.fit_note: Also acknowledges the topic is rapidly evolving (P54 flavour) without committing to review.

units.why: "If you use AI tools to search for sources, verify that they are legitimate and that they are right for your research." Permits AI source-finding on condition of verification, P104.
units.anchor: If you use AI tools to search for sources, verify that they are legitimate
units.frag_start: If you use AI tools to

units.why: The AI ROBOT Test "prompts users to consider questions related to a tool's reliability, objective, bias, ownership, type". It is a recommended instrument for assessing a tool before use, P117.
units.anchor: prompts users to consider questions related to a tool's reliability, objective, bias

units.why: Points to the "Ithaka S+R Generative AI Product Tracker", "A living document" of products, as a resource for choosing tools. It supports tool selection (P117) by referring readers to an outside resource.
units.anchor: A living document, updated regularly
units.fit_note: Mainly a pointer to an external resource (P115).

units.why: "Many AI platforms collect user data and chats to further train their models." A privacy fact that grounds data-protection advice, P50, informs.
units.anchor: Many AI platforms collect user data and chats to further train their models

units.why: "Check your account settings to see if you can opt out of data collection and training" is advice to protect personal data, P50.
units.anchor: Check your account settings to see if you can opt out of data collection

units.why: "If you are using a free account, you may have little to no privacy and data protection" warns of weaker protection on free tools, P50.
units.anchor: you may have little to no privacy and data protection
units.frag_start: If you are using a free

units.why: Calls Gemini "a safer AI tool" because Vassar-account interactions "are not shared outside of the college", while noting chats "cannot be deleted". This steers students to a vetted campus tool, P50 (prefer vetted tools), not a mandate.
units.anchor: Gemini is considered a safer AI tool
units.fit_note: Also a campus-licensed tool (P92) but only described as safer, not required or recommended outright.

units.why: "Need help with your research? Ask a Librarian!" directs students to human librarians for help, P72.
units.anchor: Need help with your research? Ask a Librarian!
units.fit_note: General research help, not specific to AI.

notes: Thin library guide; no school or computing policy found; course layer deferred.
